recheck.why: Lint is 1.000/clean, 260 lines, role/level exact, and the DV content is mostly strong and correct (per_instance type-vs-instance trap, at_least/auto_bin_max, toggle-is-bus-width, exclusions move the denominator, formal reachability as a legitimate exclusion source, "a run that passed with its checkers off is invisible to all three counts"). Budget accounting is honest and matches the steps: Glob 3+2 = 5/5, Grep 3+1+2+1+2+4 = 13 itemised of 14, Read 1+3+2 = 6 of 8. But two defects bite on first use. (1) Step 7 and the `excl count` field demand a number the procedure cannot produce: it itemises a Grep for the entry pattern and one for the reason field, no owner Grep; the Grep tool has no invert match; and two ~80-line Read windows cannot survey a file the skill itself says "run to thousands" of lines. Yet the block asks for "n of those carrying a reason and an owner" and the step asks for "an entry with neither is the finding" -- both joint/complement counts that marginal counts cannot yield. Even spending the single spare Grep on an owner pattern gives N, R, O and never the intersection. That is a step that cannot be carried out inside the skill's own caps. (2) Step 2 leaves the skill's own registered join-key field unassignable in a common case: the "c below b" bullet (killed job, full filesystem, collection off for one configuration) assigns no `inputs:` token, while `passing-only` is explicitly reserved to "c equal to b" and `unknown` to a missing identifier -- so a merge that dropped a database has no legal value, and the Human-verification line "`inputs` says which case holds" assumes one exists. Worse, the tree keys `includes-failing` on "c above b", which is the arithmetic the same paragraph forbids for `passing-only` ("a missing database and a merged failure cancel exactly"): 5 databases against 10 passing rows with two merged failures lands in the no-token bullet whose only text is "databases are missing". Also material: the prep paragraph "Four pack-wide facts come from _shared/team-profile.md" has the wrong membership -- it names Coverage output, which no step spends (it is named only to be excluded: "neither the Merge log nor the export"), and omits the Area-to-owner map, which step 6's hole block does spend at line 179, so a reader who fills only the four named profile rows hits an unfilled map. The file is untracked, so I could not diff against the previous revision; findings below are stated against the text as it stands.
remaining: BLOCKER, step 7 + step 8 block: `excl count : <n entries, n added since the archive, n of those carrying a reason and an owner>` is not derivable from the step's own retrieval. Step 7 itemises 'One Grep for the exclusion entry pattern, one for its reason field' and no owner Grep; the Grep tool has no invert flag, so 'an entry with neither is the finding' cannot be counted either, and two ~80-line Read windows cannot cover a file the skill calls thousands of lines. Either add an owner Grep and a combined reason-and-owner pattern to the budget (budget line 3 then reads 14/14 with no spare), or downgrade the field to what two counts can honestly give: total entries, entries whose line carries a reason, and 'owner coverage not counted -- N windows read'.

BLOCKER, step 2: the 'c below b' bullet assigns no `inputs:` token, so the field this skill holds in _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md is blank for the commonest anomaly (missing databases). Add a token (e.g. `inputs: incomplete`, which then also needs adding to the step 8 enum and to the Human-verification bullet) or state explicitly that c<b with every merged identifier matching a passing row still earns `passing-only` and that the shortfall is carried on the `merged` line.

BLOCKER-adjacent, step 2: `includes-failing` is keyed on the count comparison 'c above b' while `passing-only` is explicitly forbidden from being read off counts. Re-key `includes-failing` on the same identifier join ('one or more merged identifiers match a row the summary does not mark passing'), so the cancellation case the step itself warns about routes correctly instead of falling into the c<b bullet.

Step-by-step prep list is wrong in membership: 'Four pack-wide facts come from _shared/team-profile.md' names Coverage output (unspent -- mentioned only to disambiguate) and omits Area to owner map (spent by step 6's `owner` line). Name the map, and either spend Coverage output or move it into the same 'not this' clause as Merge log without counting it as one of the facts to fill.

Two slot sub-clauses are never spent, so they send the reader to interrupt a colleague for nothing: Merge log's 'and how long those are kept' (no step uses retention -- step 7 compares the archived report and summary, not an archived merge log), and Metric set's 'the per-metric target this block signs off against' (step 5 says the slot records it, but no step and no report field ever compares a metric to its target; step 8's `per metric` carries numbers only). Either add a target comparison to `per metric` / the Done-when, or drop both sub-clauses.

Step 6: `unreachable` and `not-implemented` get no separation test and no artifact the procedure opens can decide between them, yet they route to opposite places (exclusion file with a reason and an owner vs a schedule item). Reasons 1 and 4 get an explicit test ('partial coverage anywhere proves it sampled'); 2 vs 5 gets none. Add the test or say plainly that separating them is a question for the block owner and mark the token provisional.

Step 4 wording is technically off in its first clause: 'one merge across all of them makes a bin unreachable everywhere look like a hole and a bin reachable only in a configuration nobody ships look like coverage'. A bin unreachable in every configuration reads as a hole in a per-config view too -- only an exclusion fixes that, and step 6 says so. The hazard per-config totals actually fix is the mirror of the second clause: a bin the shipped configuration never reaches reading as covered because another configuration hit it. The second half is right; the first half attributes a non-config hazard to config merging.

Step 7 / step 8 label precision: 'n added since the archive' is what the count-vs-count method cannot give -- two counts yield a net delta (3 added and 1 retired reads as +2). The prose does distinguish the two methods and says 'say which you did'; the field label should match, e.g. 'n net against the archive by count, or n named additions by pattern -- say which'.

_shared/handoff-vocabulary.md drift (fix belongs in the shared file, not necessarily here): `reason` is recorded as held by dv-coverage-merge-report meaning 'Why a run was excluded from the merge', but the skill uses it for why a coverage bin reads as uncovered (`no-stimulus | unreachable | config-not-merged | never-sampled | not-implemented`). The holder is right and no other skill uses `reason:`, so nothing collides, but a reader reconciling pasted blocks against that note is told the column is about runs.

Budget headroom, worth noting rather than fixing: the single unitemised 14th Grep is already claimed by step 7's optional 'Grepping for entries the archive's list does not name'. Any Grep added for the owner count puts step 7 at or over the cap, so fixing the excl-count blocker requires raising the cap or dropping the optional check.
new_problems: Step 2's four-bullet tree is internally inconsistent in a way that reads as recent rewriting: it forbids reading `passing-only` off arithmetic ('a missing database and a merged failure cancel exactly') while still keying `includes-failing` on 'c above b', and it leaves the third bullet with no token at all.
The 'Four pack-wide facts' paragraph enumerates the wrong four: it spends prose on Coverage output, which no step uses, and omits the Area-to-owner map, which step 6's hole block does use.
`excl count` in the step 8 block asks for a reason-and-owner intersection that step 7's itemised Greps (entry pattern + reason field, no owner) structurally cannot produce.
